claims.statement: CBAM's definitive regime has applied since 1 January 2026; importers over the 50-tonne threshold need authorized-declarant status, embedded-emissions declarations, and certificates.
Importers now buy CBAM certificates and must substantiate embedded emissions, creating both certificate spend and paid supplier-data collection work.
The likely payer is an import, customs, procurement, or sustainability budget owner at a mid-market importer; service price tolerance is unknown.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Customs, procurement, finance, or sustainability director
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Customs brokers and ESG suites can bundle filing; supplier chasing and auditable data provenance are the wedge
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with EU mid-market importers
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Customs brokers, freight forwarders, trade associations, and targeted importer lists

fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Implementation fee upfront and annual platform/managed-service fee
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 50-70% after carbon specialist review and supplier operations
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 60-250 hours for initial supplier onboarding depending on portfolio
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Carbon-methodology review, professional liability, security, and multilingual supplier support
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Annual base fee plus supplier or shipment tier
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Supplier outreach, verification support, registry operations, and specialist review

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Customs brokers and enterprise ESG vendors extend CBAM modules down-market
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current certificate purchases, consultant fees, and staff time obtaining and validating embedded-emissions data from non-EU suppliers
commercial_mechanics.payer: EU importer of iron, steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, electricity, or hydrogen above applicable threshold
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Authorization filing, supplier-data gaps, first certificate forecast, or customs-broker escalation
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual CBAM declaration cycle and ongoing shipment updates

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes many small importers.
Customs brokers may already own the trusted relationship.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed data-rights and service agreement authorizing supplier outreach and emissions-document storage; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Provide importer-side templates and gap analysis without contacting suppliers or holding source documents
critical_control_point.current_owner: Importers and their non-EU suppliers control commercial and emissions data
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with EU mid-market importers
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No importer or supplier data rights are presently held
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business after importer mandate; suppliers remain source-data controllers
critical_control_point.subject: Auditable supplier emissions-data collection mandate

economics.acquisition_route: Offer a fixed-fee supplier-data gap audit to five importers, then convert one to managed collection and registry preparation
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 150 importers at 60,000 PLN annual revenue yields 9m PLN ARR; with 15-25% owner earnings and retained equity, 5m PLN founder net worth is plausible in 6-9 years. Sales cycles, specialist costs, and liability remain unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly initially; supplier operations require early hiring
economics.gross_margin_basis: Managed-service revenue less multilingual operations and carbon-methodology review
economics.payback: Assumption: 12 months at 15,000 PLN acquisition cost and 1,500 PLN monthly contribution
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual declarations with continuous shipment and supplier updates

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Supplier response benchmarks, validated document mappings, and multilingual playbooks
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays for supplier-data work and to control CBAM certificate exposure
fingerprint.problem_trigger: CBAM moved from transitional reporting to certificate-bearing definitive operation

founder_fit: Data validation and financial modeling fit the founder's skills.
Can start as a scoped analytical service before software investment.
Partner distribution can reduce high-energy direct selling.
risks: Supplier nonresponse can make delivery uneconomic.
Brokers and ESG platforms have stronger distribution.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: cross border embedded emissions data operations
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: permissioned supplier document and provenance ledger

thesis: CBAM's shift to certificate-bearing operation converts messy supplier emissions data from a reporting nuisance into a cash-exposure workflow.
title: CBAM Supplier Data Desk
uncertainties: Polish and regional importer counts above threshold are unknown.
Required verifier involvement and insurance cost are unknown.
